overview.description: Run transcription and translation outside a living cell, in a crude extract or the reconstituted PURE system. With no membrane and no growth to worry about, cell-free is fast to prototype, tolerant of toxic products, and can be freeze-dried into portable biosensors.
objectives: run a TX-TL reaction expressing a reporter from added DNA
prototype a genetic circuit cell-free in hours, not days
know when cell-free beats in-vivo expression (toxicity, speed, control)

steps.description: Add DNA (plasmid or linear PCR product) to an extract plus energy mix, incubate, and read the reporter - no transformation, no culturing.
steps.intro: Cell-free turns gene expression into a pipetting reaction: template + extract + energy + amino acids in a tube, output in a plate reader within hours.
tools: cell extract or PURE system (e.g. myTXTL)

instructions.title: Prepare template
instructions.description: Use a plasmid or a linear PCR product with a strong promoter/RBS; linear templates are quick but degrade faster.

instructions.title: Assemble the reaction
instructions.description: Combine extract, energy mix, and template on ice; keep reactions small (a few uL) and set up replicates + a no-DNA control.

instructions.title: Incubate & read
instructions.description: Incubate at ~29-37 C and track reporter signal in real time on a plate reader.

instructions.title: Prototype or preserve
instructions.description: Iterate circuit variants rapidly, or freeze-dry reactions onto paper for a portable biosensor.

submission.description: Design a cell-free experiment that expresses a reporter from your DNA, including the controls, and explain why cell-free is the right choice for your application.

resources.title: Pardee et al. - paper-based freeze-dried synthetic biology
